studentDefinition: When liquid water turns into water vapor (a gas) and goes up into the air
technicalDefinition: The process by which water changes from liquid to gas or vapor
exampleSentence: The puddle disappeared because of evaporation from the sun's heat.

studentDefinition: When water vapor (gas) cools down and turns into tiny water droplets
technicalDefinition: The process by which water vapor changes to liquid water
exampleSentence: Condensation happens when water vapor in the air forms clouds.

studentDefinition: Water that falls from clouds to the ground (like rain or snow)
technicalDefinition: Any form of water that falls from clouds to Earth's surface
exampleSentence: Rain is a type of precipitation that helps plants grow.

studentDefinition: When water gathers together in oceans, lakes, rivers, or underground
technicalDefinition: The accumulation of water in bodies of water on Earth's surface or underground
exampleSentence: After rain falls, water collection happens in rivers and lakes.

studentDefinition: Water in gas form that you can't see (it's in the air around us)
technicalDefinition: Water in its gaseous state
exampleSentence: Water vapor is invisible, but it's all around us in the air.

studentDefinition: Matter that has a definite shape and stays in place (like ice)
technicalDefinition: A state of matter with a definite shape and volume
exampleSentence: Ice is water in its solid form.

studentDefinition: Matter that can pour and take the shape of its container (like water)
technicalDefinition: A state of matter with a definite volume but no definite shape
exampleSentence: Water is a liquid that we drink and use every day.

studentDefinition: Matter that spreads out to fill any space (like steam or air)
technicalDefinition: A state of matter with no definite shape or volume
exampleSentence: Steam from boiling water is water in gas form.

studentDefinition: A collection of tiny water droplets floating in the sky
technicalDefinition: A visible mass of water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere
exampleSentence: White fluffy clouds are made of millions of tiny water droplets.

studentDefinition: Water drops that fall from clouds when they get too heavy
technicalDefinition: Liquid precipitation that falls from clouds
exampleSentence: Rain helps plants grow and fills up lakes and rivers.

studentDefinition: Frozen water crystals that fall from clouds when it's very cold
technicalDefinition: Frozen precipitation in the form of ice crystals
exampleSentence: Snow forms when water droplets freeze in very cold clouds.

studentDefinition: Balls of ice that fall from storm clouds
technicalDefinition: Precipitation in the form of balls or lumps of ice
exampleSentence: Hail can be as small as a pea or as big as a golf ball!

studentDefinition: Frozen raindrops that are like tiny ice pellets
technicalDefinition: Precipitation consisting of ice pellets formed by freezing rain
exampleSentence: Sleet makes a tapping sound when it hits windows.

studentDefinition: The big, bright star that gives Earth light and heat
technicalDefinition: The star at the center of our solar system that provides energy to Earth
exampleSentence: The sun's heat causes water to evaporate.

studentDefinition: Energy that makes things warm or hot
technicalDefinition: Thermal energy transferred from one object to another
exampleSentence: Heat from the sun causes water to evaporate into the air.

studentDefinition: The power to make things happen or change
technicalDefinition: The capacity to do work or cause change
exampleSentence: The sun's energy powers the water cycle.

studentDefinition: Water that soaks into the ground and is stored underground
technicalDefinition: Water located beneath Earth's surface in soil pore spaces and rock fractures
exampleSentence: Some rain soaks into the ground and becomes groundwater.

studentDefinition: A huge body of salt water that covers most of Earth
technicalDefinition: A large body of salt water that covers approximately 71% of Earth's surface
exampleSentence: Oceans hold most of Earth's water and are part of the water cycle.

studentDefinition: A large body of water surrounded by land
technicalDefinition: An inland body of standing water
exampleSentence: Lakes collect rainwater and water from rivers.

studentDefinition: A large stream of water that flows toward an ocean or lake
technicalDefinition: A natural flowing watercourse
exampleSentence: Rivers carry water from mountains to oceans.
